canonical_question: Does the 4.2 at% Cr addition trigger any adverse phase transformations or embrittlement at temperatures outside room temperature testing?

question_variants.question: Does the 4.2 at% Cr addition trigger any adverse phase transformations or embrittlement at temperatures outside room temperature testing?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The provided evidence reports room temperature yield strength and fracture strain values. It does not contain data or discussion regarding phase transformations, embrittlement, or mechanical behavior at temperatures outside of room temperature testing.

answers.answer: The evidence provides yield strength and fracture strain values (1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa and 14.0 ± 2.9%) but explicitly lists test conditions as un-specified or implies room temperature in the context of the reference alloy comparison. There is no data regarding adverse phase transformations or embrittlement at temperatures outside room temperature.
answers.boundary_limitation: No evidence provided for behavior at temperatures other than room temperature.
evidence_spans: 4.2 at% Cr addition into HfMoTaTiZr led to the formation of a Laves phase, in addition to the BCC phase.
The hardness of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 is 535.8 Hv 0.3 , 56.96% higher than the reference alloy HfMoTaTiZr.
The yield strength and fracture strain of HfMoTaTiZrCr 0.5 reach 1750.6 ± 80.3 MPa and 14.0 ± 2.9%, respectively, 207.5 MPa and 20.6% higher than HfMoTaTiZr.
